title: Generate Parentheses
statement:
Given `n` pairs of parentheses, write a function to generate all combinations of well-formed parentheses.

A well-formed combination never has a closing parenthesis without a matching earlier opening one, and uses exactly `n` opening and `n` closing parentheses.

Backtrack while tracking counts of open and close parentheses used so far: you may add an open paren if you haven't used all `n`, and you may add a close paren only if it wouldn't exceed the number of opens already placed.

editorial.approach: Use backtracking with a running string and two counters: `open` (opens used) and `close` (closes used). At each step, if `open < n`, recurse by adding `(` and incrementing `open`. If `close < open`, recurse by adding `)` and incrementing `close`. When the string reaches length `2n`, it's a complete valid combination — add it to the results. Because we only ever add a close when it's guaranteed valid (close count stays below open count), every generated string is automatically well-formed, so no separate validation step is needed.
editorial.complexity: O(4^n / sqrt(n)) time (Catalan number of valid combinations) / O(n) space for recursion depth
